mainTopic: Washing and bathing on שבת and יום טוב: רב vs. שמואל on pre-heated water, רבה's practice, and the history of the rabbinic bans on bathing and sweating
overview: This amud opens by finishing a discussion from the previous daf: רבה בר בר חנה says he heard his ruling explicitly, so it does not depend on the rule of following the middle opinion. Then a new topic begins. רב says that on שבת one may wash the whole body, limb by limb, with water heated before שבת. שמואל allows only the face, hands and feet. רב survives two ברייתות by reading 'face, hands and feet' as a model for washing one part at a time, but a third ברייתא supports שמואל. רבה's version of רב, wash the whole body but leave out one limb, is refuted outright. The גמרא then asks whether רבה himself practiced that version, and answers that he followed רב's stringencies but not necessarily his leniencies. Next comes a ברייתא and a story about sweating in a sealed bathhouse on יום טוב, which was later forbidden because of 'transgressors'. בר קפרא explains the history: each permission was abused, step by step, until the final rule allowed the hot springs of טבריה but kept sweating forbidden. רבא learns that someone who breaks a rabbinic law may be called a 'transgressor', and the גמרא begins asking whose view this follows; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא retracted to רבי יהושע's view
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of a point from the previous daf: in one case רבי עקיבא changed his mind and agreed with רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא went back and adopted the position of רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a discussion that started on the previous daf. It notes that רבי עקיבא changed his mind and agreed with רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The background is the rule that when one תנא takes a middle position between two others, the הלכה follows that middle opinion. In the case cited, רבי יהושע held the middle position, and רבי עקיבא himself came around to it, which supports the rule. The bathing ruling also follows a middle opinion (רבי יהודה's), so רב יוסף wanted to know whether רבה בר בר חנה heard it directly or only worked it out from that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Over to the side of (someone's opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the tail end of a discussion from the previous daf (39b). It is not the start of a new topic, so do not try to read it on its own.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva retracted
to the position of Rabbi Yehoshua.
phrases.notes: He came around to רבי יהושע's middle position, which supports the 'middle opinion' rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר בֵּיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְגַבֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא retracted to רבי יהושע's middle position, illustrating that the compromise view is followed.

steps.title: What is wrong with learning the ruling by inference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it would matter if the ruling was only inferred from the general principle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he learned it by inference, so what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב יוסף's concern. If the ruling was learned by inference from the principle, why is that a problem?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An inference from an accepted rule is normally a valid way to reach a הלכה. So the גמרא wants to know why רב יוסף insisted on knowing whether the ruling was heard explicitly. This question sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, from a general rule

phrases.english: And if it was by inference, what of it?
phrases.notes: Why would an inference be a problem?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for רב יוסף's inquiry
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why an inferred ruling would be less reliable than one heard explicitly.

steps.title: The principle may only apply to a משנה
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the 'follow the middle opinion' rule only works when the opinions appear in a משנה, not in a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps that rule applies only in a משנה, but in a ברייתא it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The concern was that the 'middle opinion' rule might only apply to a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bathing dispute is recorded in a ברייתא, not a משנה. If the rule only works for a משנה, then an inference based on it would not prove the הלכה here. That is why it mattered whether the ruling was heard explicitly.

keyTerms.meaning: A Tannaitic teaching outside the משנה

phrases.english: Perhaps these words apply only in a Mishnah,
but in a Baraita, no.
phrases.notes: The rule might not extend to a ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִילְמָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּמַתְנִיתִין, אֲבָל בְּבָרַיְיתָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The inference might fail because the middle-opinion rule may be limited to a משנה.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה heard it explicitly
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה replies to רב יוסף that he heard the ruling explicitly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I heard it explicitly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה answers רב יוסף directly. He says the ruling was stated outright, not inferred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the concern from the previous step. Since the ruling was heard explicitly, it does not depend on the 'middle opinion' rule at all. That closes this thread.
steps.whatToRemember: The ruling that רבה בר בר חנה reported was heard explicitly. It was not inferred from the rule of following the middle opinion.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא בְּפֵירוּשׁ שְׁמִיעַ לִי.
phrases.english: He said to him: I heard it explicitly.
phrases.notes: רבה בר בר חנה to רב יוסף.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא בְּפֵירוּשׁ שְׁמִיעַ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the concern raised in step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling was heard directly, so it is reliable.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about washing with pre-heated water
steps.stepSummary: רב allows washing the whole body limb by limb on שבת with water heated before שבת. שמואל allows only face, hands and feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: Hot water heated on ערב שבת. רב said: The next day one may wash his whole body with it, limb by limb. שמואל said: They permitted washing only the face, hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins with a disagreement between two אמוראים. The question is how much of the body one may wash on שבת with water that was heated before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the water itself was heated in a permitted way, before שבת. רב allows the whole body as long as it is done one limb at a time, as an unusual way of washing. שמואל limits washing to the face, hands and feet only.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the סוגיא tests רב's position against ברייתות.

phrases.english: It was stated: Hot water that was heated on Shabbat eve,

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: לְמָחָר רוֹחֵץ בָּהֶן כׇּל גּוּפוֹ,
phrases.english: Rav said: The next day one washes his entire body with it,
limb by limb.
And Shmuel said: They did not permit washing
except his face, his hands and his feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the whole body, limb by limb. שמואל: only the face, hands and feet.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to refute רב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows the face, hands and feet but 'not his entire body', which seems to contradict רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: Hot water heated on ערב שבת, the next day one washes his face, hands and feet with it, but not his whole body. This is a refutation of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to directly contradict רב. It declares this a refutation of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches שמואל's wording, and it explicitly excludes washing the entire body. That appears to rule out רב's permission to wash the whole body.

phrases.english: They objected: Hot water that was heated on Shabbat eve,

phrases.aramaic: לְמָחָר רוֹחֵץ בָּהֶן פָּנָיו יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו
phrases.english: the next day one washes his face, hands and feet with it
but not his entire body.
A refutation of Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's view from step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's permission to wash the entire body
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly says 'not his entire body'.

steps.title: רב: 'Not the whole body' means not all at once
steps.stepSummary: רב reads the ברייתא as forbidding washing the whole body at once, while allowing it limb by limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can tell you: 'Not his whole body' means at one time, but limb by limb is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by reinterpreting the words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this reading, the ברייתא only forbids washing the whole body in one go. Washing limb by limb is still allowed, which is exactly רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: He could tell you (a defense on someone's behalf)

phrases.english: Rav could say to you:
'Not his entire body' means all at once,
but limb by limb is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not his entire body' forbids the whole body in any manner.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only forbids washing the whole body all at once.

steps.title: But the ברייתא lists only face, hands and feet
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא names specifically the face, hands and feet, which implies nothing more is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'his face, hands and feet'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב's defense. The ברייתא specifically names three body parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If washing limb by limb were allowed for the whole body, why list only the face, hands and feet? The list suggests a limit.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'his face, his hands and his feet'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 7
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Naming specific limbs implies that only those limbs are permitted.

steps.title: Face, hands and feet are a model for limb-by-limb washing
steps.stepSummary: The list means 'washing in the way one washes face, hands and feet', which is one part at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means: similar to face, hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the three body parts are given as examples of a style of washing, not as a strict limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the face, hands and feet are washed separately, so too the whole body may be washed piece by piece. The list describes the method of washing.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, in the manner of

phrases.english: Similar to his face, his hands and his feet.
phrases.notes: That is, one part at a time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the list gives the method, not the limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only these three body parts may be washed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any part may be washed, as long as it is done separately, the way these three are.

steps.title: A second ברייתא against רב
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says only face, hands and feet were permitted with water heated before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: They permitted washing with water heated on ערב שבת only the face, hands and feet!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source that seems to contradict רב. It uses the limiting word 'only'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא uses the exclusive phrase 'they only permitted'. That sounds even stronger than the first source in limiting washing to these three body parts.

phrases.english: Come and hear: They did not permit washing
with hot water that was heated on Shabbat eve
except his face, his hands and his feet!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Only' limits washing to the three body parts.

steps.title: Same answer: in the manner of face, hands and feet
steps.stepSummary: רב applies the same reading to the second ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: similar to face, hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge the same way it answered the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word 'only' is read as limiting the method of washing, one part at a time. It does not limit which body parts may be washed.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, כְּעֵין פָּנָיו יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו.
phrases.english: Here too, it means similar to his face, his hands and his feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, כְּעֵין פָּנָיו יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 using the approach of step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Only' limits which body parts may be washed.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Only' limits the method: washing one part at a time.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explicitly forbids washing the whole body even limb by limb. All the more so with water heated on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in accordance with שמואל: Hot water heated on ערב שבת, the next day one washes face, hands and feet with it, but not the whole body, even limb by limb. And needless to say, water heated on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that clearly matches שמואל's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא explicitly rules out the 'limb by limb' method, so רב's reinterpretation cannot work for it. It adds that water heated on יום טוב is certainly forbidden for this.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in accordance with him

steps.whyThisMatters: This source is clear support for שמואל.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Shmuel:
Hot water that was heated on Shabbat eve,

phrases.aramaic: לְמָחָר רוֹחֵץ בָּהֶן פָּנָיו יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו,
phrases.english: the next day one washes his face, hands and feet with it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא כׇּל גּוּפוֹ אֵבֶר אֵבֶר.
phrases.english: but not his entire body, even limb by limb.
And needless to say,
hot water that was heated on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for שמואל after רב's defenses
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that excludes washing the whole body even limb by limb

steps.title: רבה's version of רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבה reports רב's view differently: wash the whole body but leave out one limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה taught רב's ruling in this language: Hot water heated on ערב שבת, the next day, רב said: One washes his whole body with it and leaves out one limb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a different version of what רב said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the whole body may even be washed at once. The only requirement is to leave one limb unwashed as a reminder that it is שבת. This is more lenient than the 'limb by limb' version.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה מַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא דְּרַב
phrases.english: Rabba would teach this ruling of Rav
in this version:
Hot water that was heated on Shabbat eve, the next day,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: רוֹחֵץ בָּהֶן כׇּל גּוּפוֹ
phrases.english: Rav said: One washes his entire body with it
and leaves out one limb.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה מַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא דְּרַב בְּהַאי לִישָּׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate version of רב's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wash the whole body, leaving out one limb.

steps.title: All the earlier objections are raised against this version
steps.stepSummary: All the ברייתות quoted before are now raised against רבה's version of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised all these refutations against him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back all the earlier sources to challenge this new version of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this version, the 'similar to face, hands and feet' answer no longer works. Washing almost the whole body at once is nothing like washing one part at a time.

phrases.english: They raised all these refutations against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 13
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sources limit washing to face, hands and feet, and this version cannot be defended by the 'limb by limb' reading.

steps.title: רבה's version of רב is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the 'leave out one limb' version of רב is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this section by declaring that the 'leave out one limb' version of רב cannot stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered to defend רבה's version, so it is rejected. Washing the whole body at once on שבת with pre-heated water is not permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'leave out one limb' version of רב is refuted. A ברייתא supports שמואל: with water heated before שבת, only the face, hands and feet may be washed.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the challenge in step 14
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבה's version of רב, washing the whole body and leaving out one limb, is rejected.

steps.title: Did רבה practice this ruling of רב?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks אביי whether רבה acted on רב's teaching. אביי says he does not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to אביי: Does רבה act according to this teaching of רב? אביי said: I do not know.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks a practical question: did רבה actually live by the 'leave out one limb' teaching that he reported in רב's name? אביי admits he does not know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not the law itself but what רבה did in practice. רבה was the one who reported this version of רב, so it makes sense to ask whether he followed it.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to Abaye:
Does Rabba act
according to this teaching of Rav?
phrases.notes: רב's teaching here is the version reported by רבה: wash the whole body but leave out one limb.

phrases.english: He said to him: I do not know.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה מִי קָא עָבֵיד כִּשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the refutation of רבה's version of רב to asking about רבה's own practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבה personally followed the 'leave out one limb' ruling.

steps.title: Why ask? The view was already refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the question itself: obviously רבה did not follow a view that was refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his question? It is obvious that he did not act this way, since that view was refuted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's question. It says the answer is obvious, because this version of רב was just refuted in step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a view is refuted (איתותב), nobody should practice it. So asking whether רבה followed it seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: what is his question / why is he unsure?

phrases.english: What is his question?
It is obvious that he does not act this way,
since it was refuted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ? פְּשִׁיטָא דְּלָא עָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the question raised in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's question about רבה's practice.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A refuted view is obviously not practiced, so there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: Maybe רבה never heard the refutation
steps.stepSummary: Answer: perhaps רבה did not hear the refutation, so he might still have practiced it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he did not hear the refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the question. Maybe רבה never heard about the refutation, or did not find it convincing, so he could still have followed the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The refutation only matters if רבה knew about it. If he did not, his practice is a real open question.

phrases.english: Perhaps he did not hear it (the refutation).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the refutation to people who knew about it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A refuted view is obviously not practiced by anyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה may not have known of the refutation, so the question stands.

steps.title: If so, רבה surely followed רב
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: if רבה did not hear the refutation, he certainly followed רב, since אביי said רבה always followed רב except in three cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he did not hear it, then he certainly acted this way. For אביי said: In all matters the Master (רבה) acted like רב, except these three where he acted like שמואל: one may move ציצית from garment to garment, one may light from lamp to lamp, and the הלכה follows רבי שמעון about dragging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again from the other side. If רבה did not hear the refutation, there is still nothing to ask, because we know רבה always followed רב except in three listed cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's rule says רבה followed רב in everything except three cases where he followed שמואל. Bathing is not one of the three. So if רבה did not know of the refutation, he must have followed רב here too.

keyTerms.meaning: moving ציצית strings from one garment to another

phrases.english: And if he did not hear it,
he certainly acted this way.
As Abaye said:
In all matters, the Master acted like Rav,
except these three, where he acted like Shmuel.
One may transfer tzitzit from garment to garment,
and one may light from lamp to lamp,
and the halacha follows Rabbi Shimon regarding dragging!
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון permits dragging a heavy object even though it might make a groove in the ground, because that was not the intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא שְׁמִיעָא לֵיהּ וַדַּאי עָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 18 into a new challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבה's practice is an open question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since רבה followed רב everywhere except three listed cases, he must have followed רב on bathing too.

steps.title: רבה followed only רב's stringencies
steps.stepSummary: Answer: רבה followed רב's stringencies, not his leniencies. Washing with hot water is a leniency, so his practice is still unclear.
steps.simpleTranslation: He followed רב's stringencies; he did not follow רב's leniencies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing אביי's rule. רבה followed רב only when רב was strict, and this bathing ruling is a leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's rule does not prove that רבה followed רב on bathing, because the 'leave out one limb' ruling is lenient. So רב יוסף's question was a real question after all.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה followed רב's stringencies, not necessarily his leniencies. That is why it stays unclear whether he practiced the lenient bathing ruling.

phrases.english: He followed Rav's stringencies;
Rav's leniencies he did not follow.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּחוּמְרֵי דְּרַב עָבֵיד, כְּקוּלֵּי דְּרַב לָא עָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the scope of אביי's general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה followed רב in everything outside the three cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה followed רב only when רב was strict, so his practice on this lenient ruling is unknown.

steps.title: A bathhouse sealed before שבת or יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a bathhouse sealed before שבת may be used right after שבת. One sealed before יום טוב may be used on יום טוב only to sweat, then rinse in the outer room.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A bathhouse whose openings were sealed on ערב שבת: after שבת one may bathe in it right away. If its openings were sealed on ערב יום טוב: the next day one may enter and sweat, then go out and rinse in the outer room.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about bathhouses whose openings were sealed beforehand to keep the heat in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the שבת case, the ברייתא only rules on the time after שבת: one may bathe right away, since the heating was done before שבת. On יום טוב one may not bathe in the hot water, but sweating in the heat and rinsing in the outer room is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: they sealed its openings (to keep the heat in)

steps.confusionAlert: Sweating is not the same as bathing. On יום טוב one may sit in the heat and sweat, but may not wash in the hot water itself.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A bathhouse whose openings were sealed on Shabbat eve,
after Shabbat one may bathe in it immediately.
If its openings were sealed on the eve of Yom Tov,
the next day one may enter and sweat,
and go out and rinse in the outer room.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֶרְחָץ שֶׁפָּקְקוּ נְקָבָיו מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about bathhouses on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After שבת one may bathe at once. On יום טוב one may sweat and rinse in the outer room, but not bathe in the hot water.

steps.title: The incident at the בני ברק bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: A story: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא sweated on יום טוב in a sealed bathhouse and rinsed in the outer room. But that bathhouse's hot water was covered with boards.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: There was an incident in the bathhouse of בני ברק, whose openings were sealed on ערב יום טוב. The next day רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא went in, sweated there, then went out and rinsed in the outer room. However, its hot water was covered with boards.
steps.whatsHappening: A story is brought that matches the ברייתא's rule for יום טוב. Great תנאים actually did this in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story supports the leniency, but it adds a detail: the hot water was covered with boards. That might mean the leniency only applies when there is no risk of someone bathing in the hot water.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
phrases.notes: Some versions read רבי יהודה here, as in the תוספתא.

phrases.english: There was an incident in the bathhouse of Bnei Brak
whose openings were sealed on the eve of Yom Tov;

phrases.aramaic: לְמָחָר נִכְנַס רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
phrases.english: the next day Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya and Rabbi Akiva entered
and sweated in it
and went out and rinsed in the outer room.
However, its hot water was covered with boards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ברייתא's יום טוב rule with a real-life case, adding a limiting detail.
steps.raayaObject: The permission to sweat on יום טוב in a bathhouse sealed beforehand.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא in בני ברק.

steps.title: The חכמים permit it even without boards
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ruled that sweating is permitted even when the hot water is not covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the matter came before the חכמים, they said: Even if its hot water is not covered with boards, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים rule on the story. The boards are not needed; sweating is permitted either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the limit suggested by the boards in step 22. The leniency is broad: one may sweat on יום טוב in any sealed bathhouse.

phrases.english: When the matter came before the Sages,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין חַמִּין שֶׁלּוֹ
phrases.english: they said: Even if its hot water is not
covered with boards (it is permitted).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Removes the boards condition from step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sweating on יום טוב is permitted even if the hot water is uncovered.

steps.title: Later forbidden because people abused it
steps.stepSummary: Once many people began to transgress, the חכמים started forbidding even sweating.
steps.simpleTranslation: And once the transgressors grew many, they began to forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ruling changes over time. Because people abused the leniency, the חכמים forbade even sweating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sweating itself was never the problem. People used it as a cover to actually bathe in hot water, so the חכמים closed the door entirely.
steps.whatToRemember: The original law allowed sweating in a sealed bathhouse on יום טוב. Later the חכמים forbade it because people abused it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a pattern found throughout ש״ס: a leniency that is technically allowed can be taken away when people misuse it.

phrases.english: And once the transgressors increased,
they began to prohibit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overrides the earlier leniency with a later prohibition.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Sweating in a heated bathhouse on יום טוב (and שבת) became forbidden because of widespread abuse.

steps.title: Strolling through large city bathhouses is allowed
steps.stepSummary: Even after the prohibition, one may walk through the large bathhouses of the cities without worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: The large bathhouses of the cities: one may stroll through them and need not be concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an exception to the new prohibition. Simply walking through a big city bathhouse is fine, even if one sweats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition targeted going in on purpose to sweat. Passing through a large public bathhouse is ordinary walking, so the חכמים did not forbid it.

phrases.english: The large bathhouses of the cities —
one may stroll through them and need not be concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְבַּטְיָאוֹת שֶׁל כְּרַכִּין מְטַיֵּיל בָּהֶן וְאֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the prohibition of step 24 with an exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Walking through large city bathhouses is permitted despite the prohibition on sweating.

steps.title: What does 'transgressors' mean here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of 'transgression' the earlier ברייתא was referring to when it said people began to transgress.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'transgressors'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the words 'עוברי עבירה' from step 24. This sets up the long historical answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said the חכמים banned sweating because many people 'transgressed', but it never said what they did wrong. The גמרא wants to know exactly what the misbehavior was.

keyTerms.meaning: transgressors; people who violate a prohibition
what is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What is meant by 'transgressors'?
phrases.notes: Quoting the phrase from the ברייתא in step 24.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the word 'transgressors' from step 24 and asks for an explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly were the people doing wrong that made the חכמים ban sweating?

steps.title: Stage one: bathhouse workers lied, so hot-water bathing was banned
steps.stepSummary: Bathing on שבת in water heated before שבת was first allowed. Bathhouse attendants then heated water on שבת and claimed it was heated earlier, so the חכמים banned hot water and allowed only sweating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said it in the name of בר קפרא: At first, people bathed on שבת in hot water that had been heated before שבת. Then the bathhouse attendants began heating water on שבת and saying, 'It was heated before שבת.' So the חכמים banned bathing in hot water and allowed sweating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering with a history lesson. The first stage shows that a lenient rule was abused, so the חכמים made it stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heating water on שבת is real חילול שבת. The attendants used the permission to bathe in water heated before שבת as a cover story. To shut down the lie, the חכמים banned hot-water bathing altogether and left only sweating permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the pattern of the whole story: every permission becomes an excuse, so the חכמים close it.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of bar Kappara:
phrases.notes: A chain of three names passing on the teaching.

phrases.english: At first, people would bathe
in hot water that was heated before Shabbat.
The bathhouse attendants began to heat water on Shabbat,
and they would say: 'It was heated before Shabbat.'

phrases.aramaic: אָסְרוּ אֶת הַחַמִּין וְהִתִּירוּ אֶת הַזֵּיעָה.
phrases.english: So they banned hot water and permitted sweating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The transgression began with attendants heating water on שבת and lying about it, which led to the ban on hot water.

steps.title: Stage two: 'We're just sweating' becomes an excuse, so sweating is banned
steps.stepSummary: People kept bathing in hot water and claimed they were only sweating. The חכמים then banned sweating too and allowed the natural hot springs of טבריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: People still bathed in hot water and said, 'We are only sweating.' So the חכמים banned sweating and allowed the hot springs of טבריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The new permission to sweat was abused, so the חכמים closed that too and gave a different permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sweating gave people a reason to be in the bathhouse, and they used it to hide forbidden bathing. The חכמים swapped it for the springs of טבריה. That water is naturally hot and was not heated by fire, so it carries no fear of heating on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the natural hot springs of טבריה

phrases.english: And they would still bathe in hot water
and say: 'We are sweating.'
So they banned sweating for them
and permitted the hot springs of Tiberias.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the history. The sweating permission from step 27 is abused and then withdrawn.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'transgressors' in step 24 were people who used sweating as a cover for forbidden bathing, which led to the ban on sweating.

steps.title: Stage three: false 'טבריה' claims lead to allowing only cold water
steps.stepSummary: People bathed in fire-heated water and claimed it was the springs of טבריה. So the חכמים banned even the springs of טבריה and allowed only cold water.
steps.simpleTranslation: People still bathed in water heated by fire and said, 'We bathed in the springs of טבריה.' So the חכמים banned the springs of טבריה too and allowed only cold water.
steps.whatsHappening: The pattern repeats a third time. The טבריה permission is abused, so the חכמים become as strict as possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a fully permitted kind of hot water became a cover story for water heated by fire. The חכמים then removed every hot-water option and left only cold water.

phrases.english: And they would still bathe in water heated by fire,
and say: 'We bathed in the hot springs of Tiberias.'
So they banned the hot springs of Tiberias for them
and permitted them cold water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the history. The טבריה permission from step 28 is abused and then withdrawn.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: People falsely claimed to use טבריה water, which led to a ban on all hot water.

steps.title: Final balance: טבריה springs allowed again, sweating stays banned
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים saw that the public could not keep such a strict rule. They allowed the springs of טבריה again but kept the ban on sweating.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים saw that the people could not keep this rule. So they permitted them the springs of טבריה again, and the ban on sweating stayed in place.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the final, settled rule. The חכמים pulled back from the extreme position to one the public could actually keep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A decree that people cannot keep is not effective, so the חכמים allowed טבריה water again. They kept the ban on sweating, which matches step 24, where sweating was forbidden because of the 'transgressors'.

keyTerms.meaning: the matter was not upheld by them; they could not keep it
remains in its place; stays in force

steps.whatToRemember: Final rule: on שבת the natural hot springs of טבריה are permitted, but sweating in a bathhouse remains forbidden. This happened because people kept abusing each permission.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the final rule is 'only cold water'. That was a temporary stage. The final rule brought back טבריה springs, while the sweating ban stayed.

phrases.english: They saw that the matter was not being kept by them,
so they permitted them the hot springs of Tiberias,
and the ban on sweating remained in place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the history by softening the extreme stage of step 29 into a final, workable rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Natural hot springs of טבריה are permitted on שבת, and sweating remains forbidden. This explains the ban on sweating in step 24.

steps.title: רבא: a violator of a rabbinic law may be called a transgressor
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from this story that someone who violates a rabbinic decree may be called an 'עבריינא' (transgressor).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A person who violates a rule of the רבנן may be called a 'transgressor'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws a general lesson from the word 'transgressors' used about the bathers. Those bathers were breaking rabbinic decrees, not Torah laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bathing bans were rabbinic, yet the ברייתא still called the violators 'עוברי עבירה'. So the title 'transgressor' is not only for people who break Torah laws. It also fits someone who breaks a rabbinic law.

keyTerms.meaning: who violates the words of the רבנן

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the seriousness of rabbinic law. Breaking a rabbinic decree still makes a person a real 'transgressor'.

phrases.english: Rava said:
One who violates the words of the Rabbis,
it is permitted to call him a 'transgressor.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי מַאן דְּעָבַר אַדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a general rule out of the word 'transgressors' that was just explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who violates a rabbinic decree may be called an 'עבריינא'.

steps.title: Whose opinion does רבא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to ask which earlier authority רבא's ruling matches.
steps.simpleTranslation: In accordance with whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move by asking which תנא agrees with רבא. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling a rabbinic violator a 'transgressor' could be a matter of debate. So the גמרא looks for an older source that supports רבא's view.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
phrases.notes: The question continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind רבא's ruling in step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא or earlier source supports רבא's ruling that a rabbinic violator may be called a transgressor?
